igcse-0580-proportion-direct-linear.description: Translate direct proportion into an equation, determine the multiplier and use it to find another value.

sections.title: What does the proportional symbol tell us?
sections.label: Translate and find the constant
sections.intro: The symbol \(\propto\) says there is a fixed multiplying relationship. It is not an equals sign.

blocks.html: \(y\propto x\) gives \(y=kx\). Use one non-zero input and its output to find \(k=\frac yx\).

figure.alt: A straight line through the origin passes through the marked pairs (2, 6) and (4, 12).
figure.caption: Doubling the input doubles the output along this line. Both labelled pairs have the same output-to-input ratio.

blocks.title: Find the constant of proportionality
blocks.prompt: \(y\) is directly proportional to \(x\). When \(x=7\), \(y=\frac{91}{2}\). Find the positive constant of proportionality \(k\) in \(y=k\,x\).
blocks.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto x\) mean \(y=k\,x\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=7\) and \(y=\frac{91}{2}\).

Divide \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{91}{2}\div 7=\frac{13}{2}\).

The model is \(y=\frac{13}{2}\,x\).
blocks.hint: Translate the words into the correct multiplication or division model before using the known pair.

retry.feedback: Divide the observed y by its transformed input to find k.

blocks.html: Finding a multiplier means dividing by the input. Taking the difference between the numbers gives a different relationship.

blocks.title: Predict a new output
blocks.prompt: \(y\) is directly proportional to \(x\). When \(x=10\), \(y=190\). Find \(y\) when \(x=12\). Give an exact answer.
blocks.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto x\) mean \(y=k\,x\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=10\) and \(y=190\).

Divide \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{190}{10}=19\).

\(y=19\times 12=228\).

The exact output is \(228\).
blocks.hint: Use the worked pair to calculate the constant. Keep it unchanged when substituting the new value.

blocks.html: Write the equation with the value of k substituted into it before using a second pair.

sections.title: How can I work backwards or predict a scale change?
sections.label: Use or undo the multiplier
sections.intro: The same \(k\) is used for every related pair. Choose whether the new question gives the input or the output.

blocks.html: For a new \(x\), multiply by \(k\). For a new \(y\), divide by \(k\). For positive values, a scale factor on \(x\) acts unchanged on \(y\).

blocks.title: Work backwards to a new input
blocks.prompt: \(y\) is directly proportional to \(x\). When \(x=4\), \(y=64\). Find the positive value of \(x\) when \(y=96\). Give an exact answer.
blocks.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto x\) mean \(y=k\,x\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=4\) and \(y=64\).

Divide \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{64}{4}=16\).

Rearrange to isolate the transformed input. \(x=\frac{96}{16}=6\).

Undo the transformation to find the positive input. \(x=6\).
blocks.hint: Use the worked pair to calculate the constant. Keep it unchanged when substituting the new value.

blocks.html: Using the new pair to change the multiplier would define a different model.

blocks.title: Use a scale factor to predict the change
blocks.prompt: \(y\) is directly proportional to \(x\). The initial pair is \(x=7\) and \(y=\frac{189}{4}\). The value of \(x\) is then multiplied by \(4\). By what factor is \(y\) multiplied?
blocks.solution:
The factor applying to the transformed input is \(4\).

The transformed input is multiplied by a constant, so the same factor applies to the output.

The resulting scale factor for \(y\) is \(4\).
blocks.hint: Transform the input scale factor according to the stated power or root. Take the reciprocal for inverse proportion.

blocks.html: Start with a direction check. A larger positive input should produce a larger output with positive k.

sections.title: How do I know a table fits the direct model?
sections.label: Check the same ratio
sections.intro: Direct proportion to \(x\) gives a graph through the origin when zero is included. The table can check the same fact at non-zero inputs.

blocks.html: Calculate the output divided by the input for more than one pair. The same ratio should result each time.

blocks.title: Recognise the correct equation
blocks.prompt: \(y\) is directly proportional to \(x\). When \(x=14\), \(y=\frac{147}{2}\). Which equation uses the right type of proportion and the value of \(k\) from the pair?
blocks.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto x\) mean \(y=k\,x\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=14\) and \(y=\frac{147}{2}\).

Divide \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{147}{2}\div 14=\frac{21}{4}\).

Substitute the value of \(k\) into the matching model. \(y=\frac{21}{4}\,x\).
blocks.hint: Translate the words into the correct multiplication or division model before using the known pair.

blocks.html: Two increasing quantities need not be directly proportional. If the ratio varies, this model does not fit.

igcse-0580-proportion-inverse-linear.description: Recognise a fixed product, calculate the constant and predict the effect of changing a positive input.

sections.title: Which part stays constant in inverse proportion?
sections.label: Multiply the two known values
sections.intro: In an inverse model with positive values, one quantity falls as the other rises. The product stays fixed.

blocks.html: \(y\propto\frac1x\) gives \(y=\frac{k}{x}\). Multiplying by \(x\) shows that \(xy=k\).

figure.alt: A decreasing curve passes through (2, 6), (3, 4) and (6, 2). The axes do not meet the curve.
figure.caption: Each plotted pair has product 12. A larger positive input makes the output smaller.

blocks.title: Find the constant of proportionality
blocks.prompt: \(y\) is inversely proportional to \(x\). When \(x=7\), \(y=\frac{13}{14}\). Find the positive constant of proportionality \(k\) in \(y=\frac{k}{x}\).
blocks.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto \frac{1}{x}\) mean \(y=\frac{k}{x}\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=7\) and \(y=\frac{13}{14}\).

Multiply \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{13}{14}\times7=\frac{13}{2}\).

The model is \(y=\frac{13}{2\,x}\).
blocks.hint: Translate the words into the correct multiplication or division model before using the known pair.

retry.feedback: The input transformation is in the denominator. Multiply by it to recover k.

blocks.html: Dividing the observed y by x gives a direct-model multiplier. For inverse proportion to x use their product.

blocks.title: Predict a new output
blocks.prompt: \(y\) is inversely proportional to \(x\). When \(x=10\), \(y=\frac{19}{10}\). Find \(y\) when \(x=12\). Give an exact answer.
blocks.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto \frac{1}{x}\) mean \(y=\frac{k}{x}\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=10\) and \(y=\frac{19}{10}\).

Multiply \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{19}{10}\times10=19\).

\(y=\frac{19}{12}=\frac{19}{12}\).

The exact output is \(\frac{19}{12}\).
blocks.hint: Use the worked pair to calculate the constant. Keep it unchanged when substituting the new value.

blocks.html: Keep x positive in these models. The denominator cannot be zero.

sections.title: How does the new factor affect the output?
sections.label: Use the reciprocal change
sections.intro: The same value of \(k\) connects every pair. A bigger denominator divides the constant into smaller values.

blocks.html: If \(x\) is multiplied by a factor \(c\), \(y\) is divided by \(c\). When finding \(x\) from a given \(y\), use \(x=\frac ky\).

blocks.title: Work backwards to a new input
blocks.prompt: \(y\) is inversely proportional to \(x\). When \(x=4\), \(y=4\). Find the positive value of \(x\) when \(y=\frac{8}{3}\). Give an exact answer.
blocks.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto \frac{1}{x}\) mean \(y=\frac{k}{x}\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=4\) and \(y=4\).

Multiply \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=4\times4=16\).

Rearrange to isolate the transformed input. \(x=16\div \frac{8}{3}=6\).

Undo the transformation to find the positive input. \(x=6\).
blocks.hint: Use the worked pair to calculate the constant. Keep it unchanged when substituting the new value.

blocks.html: Doubling the input would halve the output. Adding or subtracting a fixed amount does not describe the scaling rule.

blocks.title: Use a scale factor to predict the change
blocks.prompt: \(y\) is inversely proportional to \(x\). The initial pair is \(x=7\) and \(y=\frac{27}{28}\). The value of \(x\) is then multiplied by \(4\). By what factor is \(y\) multiplied?
blocks.solution:
The factor applying to the transformed input is \(4\).

Since the transformed input is in the denominator, take its reciprocal.

The resulting scale factor for \(y\) is \(\frac{1}{4}\).
blocks.hint: Transform the input scale factor according to the stated power or root. Take the reciprocal for inverse proportion.

retry.feedback: The transformed factor applies to the denominator. Use its reciprocal.

blocks.html: In a fixed total-work model, increasing the positive work rate should shorten the time.

sections.title: How do I distinguish a fixed product from a fixed ratio?
sections.label: Compare more than one pair
sections.intro: Direct proportion to x keeps the output-to-input ratio fixed. Inverse proportion to x keeps the product fixed.

blocks.html: Test the same quantity with two supplied pairs. If the products match, use that value of \(k\) in the inverse equation.

igcse-0580-proportion-direct-powers.description: Square or cube the input before using the constant, and reverse the transformation to find a positive input.

sections.title: What exactly gets squared or cubed?
sections.label: Translate the named power
sections.intro: Read the power in the relationship before using the pair. A comparable shape may scale by a power of its length.

blocks.html: Write \(y=kx^2\) for direct proportion to the square and \(y=kx^3\) for the cube. First work out the power of the known input, then divide the known output by it.

figure.alt: The square and cube curves agree at (1, 1). At x equals 2, the cube gives 8 and the square gives 4.
figure.caption: The cube curve rises faster after the common point at input 1.

blocks.title: Find the constant of proportionality
blocks.prompt: \(y\) is directly proportional to the square of \(x\). When \(x=7\), \(y=\frac{637}{2}\). Find the positive constant of proportionality \(k\) in \(y=k\,x^2\).
blocks.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto x^2\) mean \(y=k\,x^2\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=7\) and \(y=\frac{637}{2}\). \(\left(7\right)^2=49\).

Divide \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{637}{2}\div 49=\frac{13}{2}\).

The model is \(y=\frac{13}{2}\,x^2\).
blocks.hint: Translate the words into the correct multiplication or division model before using the known pair.

retry.feedback: Divide the observed y by its transformed input to find k.

blocks.html: Putting the constant inside the power would raise the constant to that power as well.

blocks.title: Predict a new output
blocks.prompt: \(y\) is directly proportional to the cube of \(x\). When \(x=10\), \(y=19000\). Find \(y\) when \(x=12\). Give an exact answer.
blocks.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto x^3\) mean \(y=k\,x^3\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=10\) and \(y=19000\). \(\left(10\right)^3=1000\).

Divide \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{19000}{1000}=19\).

\(y=19\times \left(12\right)^3=32832\).

The exact output is \(32832\).
blocks.hint: Use the worked pair to calculate the constant. Keep it unchanged when substituting the new value.

retry.feedback: Find the exact power or root of x before using the constant.

blocks.html: Write the transformed input first. It makes mistakes in the value of k easier to spot.

sections.title: How can I reverse the model or check a scale factor?
sections.label: Undo the same power
sections.intro: Before taking a root, isolate the expression in \(x\). Use the positive value of \(x\) in the measurement contexts on this page.

blocks.html: In a square model, first isolate and take the positive square root of \(x^2\). In a cube model, take the cube root after finding \(x^3\). If the problem specifies a bracket such as \((x+1)^2\), take the root before subtracting 1. For unshifted powers, doubling x gives factors 4 and 8.

blocks.title: Work backwards to a new input
blocks.prompt: \(y\) is directly proportional to the square of \(x+1\). Take \(x>-1\). When \(x=3\), \(y=256\). Find the positive value of \(x\) when \(y=576\). Give an exact answer.
blocks.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto \left(x+1\right)^2\) mean \(y=k\,\left(x+1\right)^2\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=3\) and \(y=256\). \(\left(3+1\right)^2=16\).

Divide \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{256}{16}=16\).

Rearrange to isolate the transformed input. \(\left(x+1\right)^2=\frac{576}{16}=36\).

Undo the power or root to isolate \(x+1\), then undo its constant shift. \(x=5\).
blocks.hint: Use the worked pair to calculate the constant. Keep it unchanged when substituting the new value.

retry.feedback: This is the transformed input. Undo the power or root to get x.

blocks.html: The computed square or cube is not necessarily x itself.

blocks.title: Use a scale factor to predict the change
blocks.prompt: \(y\) is directly proportional to the cube of \(x\). The initial pair is \(x=7\) and \(y=\frac{9261}{4}\). The value of \(x\) is then multiplied by \(4\). By what factor is \(y\) multiplied?
blocks.solution:
The factor applying to the transformed input is \(\left(4\right)^3=64\).

The transformed input is multiplied by a constant, so the same factor applies to the output.

The resulting scale factor for \(y\) is \(64\).
blocks.hint: Transform the input scale factor according to the stated power or root. Take the reciprocal for inverse proportion.

retry.feedback: Use the power or root of the input scale factor stated in the model.

blocks.html: State the positive domain when a negative root would not be meaningful.

sections.title: How do I test a proposed equation against data?
sections.label: Keep the transformed ratio fixed
sections.intro: A successful equation uses the right power of \(x\) and the same numerical coefficient for all pairs.

blocks.html: Use the ratio \(\frac{y}{x^2}\) or \(\frac{y}{x^3}\) for each pair. The constancy of the relevant ratio is the check.

blocks.title: Recognise the correct equation
blocks.prompt: \(y\) is directly proportional to the square of \(x\). When \(x=14\), \(y=1029\). Which equation uses the right type of proportion and the value of \(k\) from the pair?
blocks.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto x^2\) mean \(y=k\,x^2\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=14\) and \(y=1029\). \(\left(14\right)^2=196\).

Divide \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{1029}{196}=\frac{21}{4}\).

Substitute the value of \(k\) into the matching model. \(y=\frac{21}{4}\,x^2\).
blocks.hint: Translate the words into the correct multiplication or division model before using the known pair.

blocks.html: The curve need not be straight. The input power, not the plain input, is proportional to y.

blocks.title: Use the constant to complete a table
blocks.prompt:
\(y\) is directly proportional to the cube of \(x\). Find the missing value of \(y\) in the last row. Give an exact answer.

\(x\)\(y\)
\(4\)\(1024\)
\(5\)\(2000\)
\(6\)Missing value
blocks.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto x^3\) mean \(y=k\,x^3\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=4\) and \(y=1024\). \(\left(4\right)^3=64\).

Divide \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{1024}{64}=16\).

The middle row gives the same constant. Use it again with the last input.

\(y=16\times \left(6\right)^3=3456\).
blocks.hint: Use the worked pair to calculate the constant. Keep it unchanged when substituting the new value.

retry.feedback: That is the output from the middle row. Use the last row’s input with the same constant.

blocks.html: Check both the earlier pair and your predicted pair against the same equation.

igcse-0580-proportion-inverse-powers.description: Use a positive squared or cubed denominator, recover the constant and compare the size of a model’s outputs.

sections.title: Which expression belongs in the denominator?
sections.label: Write the inverse power
sections.intro: The output is proportional to the reciprocal of the stated power. Evaluate the power before dividing.

blocks.html: Use \(y=\frac{k}{x^2}\) for an inverse square and \(y=\frac{k}{x^3}\) for an inverse cube. Multiply the known output by the relevant power of the known input to find k.

figure.alt: At x equals 1 the two curves have the same output. Beyond 1 the inverse-cube curve is below the inverse-square curve.
figure.caption: Both curves decrease for positive inputs. The inverse-cube model falls faster from the common point.

blocks.title: Find the constant of proportionality
blocks.prompt: \(y\) is inversely proportional to the square of \(x\). When \(x=7\), \(y=\frac{13}{98}\). Find the positive constant of proportionality \(k\) in \(y=\frac{k}{x^2}\).
blocks.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto \frac{1}{x^2}\) mean \(y=\frac{k}{x^2}\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=7\) and \(y=\frac{13}{98}\). \(\left(7\right)^2=49\).

Multiply \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{13}{98}\times49=\frac{13}{2}\).

The model is \(y=\frac{13}{2\,x^2}\).
blocks.hint: Translate the words into the correct multiplication or division model before using the known pair.

retry.feedback: The input transformation is in the denominator. Multiply by it to recover k.

blocks.html: The model uses a reciprocal power, not a negative output. The output stays positive on the positive branch.

blocks.title: Predict a new output
blocks.prompt: \(y\) is inversely proportional to the cube of \(x\). When \(x=10\), \(y=\frac{19}{1000}\). Find \(y\) when \(x=12\). Give an exact answer.
blocks.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto \frac{1}{x^3}\) mean \(y=\frac{k}{x^3}\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=10\) and \(y=\frac{19}{1000}\). \(\left(10\right)^3=1000\).

Multiply \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{19}{1000}\times1000=19\).

\(y=\frac{19}{\left(12\right)^3}=\frac{19}{1728}\).

The exact output is \(\frac{19}{1728}\).
blocks.hint: Use the worked pair to calculate the constant. Keep it unchanged when substituting the new value.

retry.feedback: Find the exact power or root of x before using the constant.

blocks.html: Brackets help when the numeric input is a fraction or decimal.

sections.title: What happens if the input changes by a known factor?
sections.label: Transform then invert
sections.intro: The change acts on the denominator. First apply the power to the input scale factor.

blocks.html: For unshifted powers, doubling the input divides inverse-square output by 4 and inverse-cube output by 8. When recovering \(x\), isolate the whole denominator and undo the power.

blocks.title: Work backwards to a new input
blocks.prompt: \(y\) is inversely proportional to the square of \(x-2\). Take \(x>2\). When \(x=6\), \(y=1\). Find the positive value of \(x\) when \(y=\frac{4}{9}\). Give an exact answer.
blocks.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto \frac{1}{\left(x-2\right)^2}\) mean \(y=\frac{k}{\left(x-2\right)^2}\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=6\) and \(y=1\). \(\left(6-2\right)^2=16\).

Multiply \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=1\times16=16\).

Rearrange to isolate the transformed input. \(\left(x-2\right)^2=16\div \frac{4}{9}=36\).

Undo the power or root to isolate \(x-2\), then undo its constant shift. \(x=8\).
blocks.hint: Use the worked pair to calculate the constant. Keep it unchanged when substituting the new value.

retry.feedback: This is the transformed input. Undo the power or root to get x.

blocks.html: Taking the reciprocal before or after the correct power leads to the same factor. Omitting the power altogether does not.

blocks.title: Use a scale factor to predict the change
blocks.prompt: \(y\) is inversely proportional to the cube of \(x\). The initial pair is \(x=7\) and \(y=\frac{27}{1372}\). The value of \(x\) is then multiplied by \(4\). By what factor is \(y\) multiplied?
blocks.solution:
The factor applying to the transformed input is \(\left(4\right)^3=64\).

Since the transformed input is in the denominator, take its reciprocal.

The resulting scale factor for \(y\) is \(\frac{1}{64}\).
blocks.hint: Transform the input scale factor according to the stated power or root. Take the reciprocal for inverse proportion.

retry.feedback: The transformed factor applies to the denominator. Use its reciprocal.

blocks.html: A positive input increase should produce a smaller positive output.

sections.title: Which product stays fixed?
sections.label: Check the transformed product
sections.intro: The product of the output and the correct input power should equal the fitted constant.

blocks.html: Check \(yx^2\) or \(yx^3\) across known pairs. With \(y=\frac{k}{(x-2)^2}\), the fixed product is \(y(x-2)^2\).

blocks.title: Recognise the correct equation
blocks.prompt: \(y\) is inversely proportional to the square of \(x\). When \(x=14\), \(y=\frac{3}{112}\). Which equation uses the right type of proportion and the value of \(k\) from the pair?
blocks.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto \frac{1}{x^2}\) mean \(y=\frac{k}{x^2}\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).

Use \(x=14\) and \(y=\frac{3}{112}\). \(\left(14\right)^2=196\).

Multiply \(y\) by the transformed value of \(x\). \(k=\frac{3}{112}\times196=\frac{21}{4}\).

Substitute the value of \(k\) into the matching model. \(y=\frac{21}{4\,x^2}\).
blocks.hint: Translate the words into the correct multiplication or division model before using the known pair.

blocks.html: Testing \(xy\) for an inverse square can make a correct table look incorrect.

blocks.title: Use the constant to complete a table
blocks.prompt:
\(y\) is inversely proportional to the cube of \(x\). Find the missing value of \(y\) in the last row. Give an exact answer.

\(x\)\(y\)
\(4\)\(\frac{1}{4}\)
\(5\)\(\frac{16}{125}\)
\(6\)Missing value
blocks.solution:
The symbols \(y\propto \frac{1}{x^3}\) mean \(y=\frac{k}{x^3}\) for a fixed multiplier \(k\).
